Prepared for Kevin Balfe

A key,
not a ticket.

One operating layer for trust, access, and revenue at ARENA.

The problem

A membership is sold on exclusivity. Exclusivity is worth what you can enforce.

Today that enforcement lives in spreadsheets, group chats, and the judgment of whoever is standing at the door. It holds until it does not, and you find out afterward.

What it does

Three jobs, one system.

  • Vets who gets in. Applicants are scored before approval. Synthetic photos, burner emails, and duplicate passports get caught in the queue, not at the gate.
  • Governs who stays in. Watchlist, restrict, reinstate. The door console hands your front desk a decision and the reason behind it on one screen.
  • Finds money you already earned. The next three pages.

The money

It reads your own data and returns gaps with dollars attached.

Not another dashboard. Four findings, each one a decision you approve or dismiss. Both are recorded.

The part that protects you

It catches what a single review never could.

Three accounts vouching for each other in a closed loop, with no outside referrer. Each application looked fine on its own. The shape only exists across all of them.

The record

Every decision signs the one before it.

The audit log is SHA-256 hash-chained. Change any historical field and that record's signature breaks, and so does every record after it. Press Verify Integrity and it re-hashes the whole chain in front of you.

There is a control on that page called Alter a record. It rewrites a historical entry to read "Access granted, approved by management," exactly what a cover-up looks like. Verify again and the console names the record that broke. That is the difference between claiming an immutable log and having one.

Why it grows the business

  • More members without more staff. Vetting that took an afternoon takes a click, with the reasoning attached.
  • Sponsors bring more people. Guests clear before the night instead of being argued about at the door, so members stop hesitating to invite.
  • Empty suites get filled, not noticed later. The gap surfaces while the fixture is still sellable.
  • The record answers for you. Insurers, partners, and members all eventually ask the same question. This answers it without a search through anyone's inbox.

It explains itself

The Tour button sits at the bottom right of every screen. It walks each tab in order with the real page underneath, so none of this has to be remembered. Arrow keys to move, escape to leave. Press Cmd-K anywhere to jump to any page, member, or applicant.

Switch desks from your name in the sidebar. Drop to Front Desk and the console reduces from twelve areas to six and opens on the door. The roles are enforced, not described.
